subject: Re: Kickoff: Wasserstein batch-effect correction as a corpus-wide layer
body:
Anders,

Resourcing:
- Umar Costa 55%, method work and the transfer study.
- Linnea Yamada 35%, preprocessing - percentile-matching normalization and the factor analysis step, i.e. the ljosa path end to end.
- Amara Okafor 30%, pipeline integration.

Compute is small, ~250 GPU-hours on titan-a100. The TensorFlow implementation is old but it runs.

Schedule dependency worth flagging: the non-imaging corpus we want for the May 29 milestone has to be re-ingested with per-run metadata attached, otherwise we have no batch labels to correct against. The Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-07-24, so we have the whole of July to land the re-ingest before anything locks; I've planned the embedding re-export backwards from 2026-07-24. That gives Amara comfortable float and means I don't need to fight anyone for priority in May.

Alina
